slides.subtitle: Claude Projects and Cowork now share memory. Here's how we set ours up so it actually holds, and what ChatGPT and Gemini do differently.

slides.label: Give every job its own Project, not one long chat
slides.detail: A Project is a separate memory space with its own files and instructions. Run five clients through one chat thread and the AI blends them. Run each through its own Project and nothing bleeds across.
slides.start: Open a Project for the client or job you re-explain the most, right now.

slides.label: Load the three documents you keep re-pasting
slides.detail: Price list, service area, standard terms. Drop them into the Project's files once and every future chat inside it already knows them, instead of you retyping the same paragraph on a Tuesday and again on a Friday.
slides.start: Add your price list, service area and terms to one Project today.

slides.label: Chat and Cowork now share the same memory
slides.detail: Since the merge in September, whatever you tell Claude in one surface shows up when you are back in the other, as long as you are in the same Project. Start a task on your phone, finish it at your desk, and it remembers where you left off.
slides.start: Switch from chat to Cowork on the same Project and check the summary carried over.

slides.label: Every tool remembers differently, and that is the trade-off
slides.detail: ChatGPT's Dreaming system now rewrites its own memory after each chat with no prompting. Gemini's Gems run on fixed instructions and knowledge files, so a new fact you mention today is gone again tomorrow unless you go back and edit the Gem by hand.
slides.start: Check which of your AI tools update themselves and which need manual edits.

slides.label: Remembering more also means storing more
slides.detail: Businesses everywhere assume their AI recognises returning customers. Consumers keep saying it still does not. Whichever tool wins that argument for you, everything it remembers is also everything it is keeping, so check the memory settings before you paste anything sensitive.
slides.start: Open your Project's memory or saved info panel and see what is actually stored.

slides.label: Test it before you trust it
slides.detail: Close the chat, open a fresh one in the same Project, and ask it something only the earlier conversation would know. If it answers correctly, the setup works. If it does not, the files or instructions need another pass.
slides.start: Run that test on your busiest recurring Project this afternoon.

title: Stop repeating yourself.
Start building on it.
slides.body: We built our own Projects around the clients and jobs we explain most often, so the AI carries the context instead of us carrying it every time.
slides.cta: Which job would you save the most time on if the AI already knew the details?
